leverage.exposure: An open leveraged position, deepening if the bid wins, and it is the only thing on this page that can cost a whole matchday. The balance is already negative and the live offer would take it substantially further under. A negative balance when the matchday locks scores ZERO for the entire matchday, so the deficit must be fully unwound before then — that is the deadline that governs everything else. The good news is that there is real time: the lock is more than two weeks out, which is why this is a scheduling problem rather than an emergency tonight. What is NOT true, and previous runs had it right, is that a negative balance blocks buying; it costs nothing until the instant of the lock. What constrains a buy is whether it can be unwound in time, and this one can — but only with two sales, not one.

binding_gap: The fourth midfielder, and the live Fernandez bid is exactly the thing that closes it. With only three midfielders the squad can field precisely one formation; a fourth opens the four-four-two that produces the best eleven in every structure worth considering. The second binding constraint, and the one that will outlast this week, is the weak fielded defender: in every unwind that leaves eleven or twelve players except one, Nakuzola is FORCED into the eleven because only four other defenders remain, and he has not started a match all season. Replacing him is worth far more fielded points than any flip on the board, and it is the first thing to do once the balance is back above water.
